label: One-word verdict fragment
description: The message opens with a single past-participle or status word punctuated as its own sentence, so the verdict lands before any evidence; reported as the dominant opener in every shard.

label: Conjoined past-participle telegraph
description: Two to five past participles chained as the whole first sentence, compressing the entire work report into a verb list with no subject; found in 14 shards.
examples: Fixed, tested, committed, pushed, and redeployed.

label: Subject-elided past-tense verb opener
description: The first word is a bare past-tense verb with the 'I' deleted, followed directly by the deliverable; the near-template 'Implemented the <adj> <noun>' recurs across all shards.
examples: Removed the auto top-up row from the Funds balance card.
Continued the compression parity work and closed another behavior gap.
Added Headroom-style fail-open protection for Tau's direct compression path.

label: Bare Yes/No verdict token
description: A one-word polarity answer punctuated as its own sentence before the real content; every shard reports it, typically 12-20 of 50 messages.

label: Affirm, then immediately qualify
description: The opening 'Yes' is reversed or fenced in the same sentence by 'but', 'with one correction', or a partial hedge, so the verdict token carries no information; 8 shards.
examples: Yes, with one important correction: **the current Hours plans do not trigger provisioning.**
Yes, but not as the current static default.

label: Concede the user was right first
description: Opens by ratifying the user's correctness or conceding an error before any content of its own; present in 15 of 18 shards.
regex: ^\s*(?:You(?:'|’)?re right|You are right|You were right|You(?:'|’)?re correct|You are correct|You are exactly right|Your (?:instinct|instincts|read|sequencing|distinction)\b)
examples: You're right. I drifted into solving the content by hand, which is the wrong move here.
You were right. My earlier read was wrong because I checked SJI first.
You're right to call this out. I had not run the seed after the prior deploy work.
Your instinct is exactly right, and the audit proves it's a real gap — not a hypothetical one.

label: Compliance token opener
description: Opens with 'Understood' / 'Acknowledged' / 'Noted' absorbing an instruction, usually followed by parroting the user's own constraint back; heavy in shards 8-18.
examples: Understood. I'll apply that verification and reporting standard on every completion claim.
Acknowledged. The verified claim remains limited to the deployed pre-close checkpoint.
Understood; subsequent completion claims will distinguish design, local implementation, runtime execution, and verified behavioral evidence.

label: Promise to behave differently next time
description: A content-free pledge about how future completion claims will be worded, standing in for doing work; whole messages in shards 15-18 consist of only this plus a coda.
regex: (?:\bI(?:'|’)?ll\s+(?:apply|keep|continue to|reconcile|limit|state)\b[^.\n]{0,140}\b(?:completion claims?|evidence|verification standard|limitations?|standard)\b|\bFuture completion (?:claims|reports) will\b|\bSubsequent completion claims will\b)
examples: Understood. I'll keep completion claims tied to exact observed evidence and state limitations plainly.
Acknowledged. Future completion reports will distinguish direct evidence from limitations and include the required turn summary.
Understood; subsequent completion claims will distinguish design, local implementation, runtime execution, and verified behavioral evidence.
Understood. I'll apply that evidence check before making any fixed, resolved, verified, or completed claim.

label: 'Reconciled:' / scope-narrowing label opener
description: An entire message genre whose first word announces that a prior claim is being narrowed, using one of a small set of interchangeable labels; 6 shards, up to 18 of 50 in one.
regex: ^\s*(?:Reconciled|Reconciliation complete|Reconciled status|Reconciled scope|Reconciled limitation|Claim reconciled|Evidence reconciled|Evidence reconciliation|Evidence clarification|Evidence boundary|Scope reconciliation|Scope check|Scope confirmed|Scope clarification|Scope limitation|Verified scope|Precision limitation|Narrowed claim|Narrowing (?:one point|the claim)|Correction(?: for precision)?|Clarification|Observed production evidence only)\b\s*[:.,]
examples: Reconciled: only the isolated local fixture was verified—not the complete canonical Observation node.
Narrowed claim: only the established-history C-X2 branch was verified.
Scope confirmed: this was a local pre-run review of the uncommitted CLD worktree.

label: First line is a colon stub introducing a list
description: The opening line is a label fragment ending in a colon that hands straight to bullets or a fence, so the message has no topic sentence; 7 shards.
examples: Evidence from the repo right now:

label: "Here's the honest status" framing sentence
description: A second sentence that announces the shape of the message instead of being part of it; every instance is deletable without loss.
examples: Here's the headline and the issues.

label: Mandatory 'Turn summary:' footer
description: A trailing paragraph literally beginning 'Turn summary:' whose first sentence restates the body verbatim-in-other-words and whose second names a next step; 48-49 of 50 in shards 16-18.
examples: Turn summary: We completed the independent adversarial audit of CHI-13.
Turn summary: The explicit CHI-16 selector is locally implemented and verified. The next best step is pushing `db79db69` to `origin/dev`.
Turn summary: The completion-check requirements are acknowledged.
Turn summary: We refined Erin into a process-governance system.

label: 'We' in the coda for solo work
description: The body says 'I' and the summary flips to 'We' for the same solo agent work, diffusing credit to a collaborator who did nothing; 24-26 codas per shard in shards 15-18.
examples: Turn summary: We confirmed from the live SMS and tool traces that Charlie failed to route.
Turn summary: We verified that DIV implements most of Phase 1.
Turn summary: We implemented the single-root SMSKit repair locally with focused contract coverage.
Turn summary: We reviewed the live quantitative process and found gaps.

label: 'Best next step:' prescription
description: A fixed terminal slot naming one future action, always superlative though there is never a runner-up; the single strongest closing tic across shards 6-18, up to 39 of 50.
examples: Best next step: fix the idea-to-story actor normalization lane first, because it accounts for multiple failures.
The next best step is to add malformed-payload non-mutation proof.
The single next best step is to leave the workspace untouched.

label: 'The next/remaining X is' forward pointer
description: Closes by naming work not done, using a fixed frame of 'the next' plus a superlative plus a work noun; 8 shards.
examples: The next real move is deployment/reset materialization, not more theory.
The next highest-value fix is to suppress SMS alerts for `cancelled` runs.
The remaining proof is to run this contract against isolated real bug artifacts.
The next major remaining work is production deployment/reset path:
The only remaining investigation is separate:

label: 'I did not X' negative disclosure
description: A standalone terminal sentence inventorying untaken actions, emitted unprompted whether or not anyone could have believed otherwise; all 18 shards.
examples: I did not run the live BASIC suite.
I did not stage, commit, push, or deploy.
I have not committed or deployed these changes yet.
I did not touch shared Engine source or CHI during this rerun.
I issued no live bug-row mutations.

label: 'Nothing was deployed' compliance recital
description: A standing attestation that no side effects occurred, appended as a ritual rather than as an answer to anything asked; 30-32 of 50 in the later shards.
examples: Nothing was committed, deployed, or exercised against live Host/CHI.
No code changes were made for this one; this was live state repair.
No production data or configuration was changed.
No tooling code was changed, deployed, or restarted.

label: Four-to-nine-noun negated enumeration
description: A long comma list of systems that were not touched, escalating the disclaimer into an inventory; 5 shards.
examples: No code, queues, tests, evals, commits, deployments, or live data were changed during this investigation.
No provider, model, MiniMax, Pipecat, voice architecture, deployment, live call, or SMS path was changed or exercised.
No code, coupon records, jobs, or customer data were changed.
No invitations, tokens, assignments, or engagement records were regenerated or changed.

label: Unrelated dirty work disclaimed and 'preserved'
description: A recurring boilerplate clause partitioning pre-existing repo mess from this turn's work, with 'preserved' or 'left untouched' as the ritual verb; 8 shards.
examples: Existing unrelated dirty work is still present in `.pi/`, `app/services/google_voice/`, and `tests/`.
The existing unrelated dirty repo files were left untouched.
The four unrelated dirty agent `pyproject.toml` files were preserved.

label: Memory/skill-file compliance citation
description: A near-final sentence naming the .md rule file that governed the run; it certifies process obedience and says nothing about the result; 11 shards.
regex: \b(?:Memory(?:/preflight| preflight| rules?| used| rule used)?|Operational(?: memory| handling| routing| details| guidance| credential| targeting| preflight| behavior| access| paths| assessment)?|Deployment(?: targeting)?|Plane used|I followed|I used|This follow(?:s|ed)|The (?:audit|rerun|deployment|process|topology|evidence-first workflow) (?:followed|used|comes from))\b[^.\n]{0,180}?\.md\b

label: Preflight that found nothing, reported anyway
description: Narrates that a memory search returned no hits — process narration with zero payload; noted in 4 shards.
examples: Memory preflight found no existing Claire alias rule.

Memory preflight found no CHI-specific retained procedure.

label: 'What changed:' section label
description: A bare noun-phrase line ending in a colon used instead of a markdown header to open the change list; the label rotates through 15+ near-synonyms doing one job. Present in all 18 shards.
regex: (?m)^\s*(?:What changed(?: in this pass| now| and shipped| back)?|What I (?:did|found|verified|observed|added|fixed)|What(?:'|’)s done|What now exists|What exists(?: now| right now)?|What happened|What we know|What is (?:actually proven|still weak|verified now|not verified enough)|Key changes|Key pieces now in place|Changed|Changes|Delivered|Implemented|Added|Removed|Key outcomes)\s*:\s*$

label: 'Verification:' evidence block
description: A near-mandatory labelled block of proof bullets that always sits after the change list and before the caveat, never integrated into prose; all 18 shards.
regex: (?m)^\s*(?:Verification(?: run| passed| done| I ran| and deploy status)?|Verified(?: live| now| on [^\n:]{0,40})?|Validation(?: passed| results| already run)?|Checks pass(?:ed)?|Smoke checks passed|Final checks|Evidence|Live proof|Current evidence|Requirements evidence|Smoke evidence|Tests(?: added| run)?)\s*:\s*$

label: Claim, colon, bullet fragments
description: Almost every claim is delivered as a stem plus an unranked bullet list of noun fragments rather than as prose; 35-48 of 50 in every shard, and Codex's only organising device.

label: 'Label: `value`' verbless bullets
description: Bullets are key-value rows wearing a dash — an identifier and its state with no verb and no article; the dominant bullet shape from shard 8 onward.

label: Bullet run where every item starts with a past-tense verb
description: Consecutive change bullets all opening with the same verb form, turning a diff into a parallel-structure inventory; 6 shards.
examples: - Closed 93 pre-`1.0.307` failed executable backlog rows as `closed_rejected`.

label: Consecutive 'No X' / 'It does not' bullets
description: Three to ten bullets that all begin with the same negative token, converting absence into a list; 5 shards.

label: Bold Title-Case line as a header
description: Invented section titles in bold Title Case standing alone on a line in place of markdown headers, often 5-11 of them in a 300-word message; 8 shards.

label: Numbered bold pseudo-headings
description: Advisory answers rendered as `1. **Title**` items with a bare bullet list under each, even in a 200-word reply; 5 shards.

label: ```text fence around non-code
description: Prose, filenames, UI labels, status lines or invented pseudo-schemas wrapped in a text fence though none of it is code; 7 shards, up to 17 fences in one message.

label: Arrow chain as a diagram substitute
description: Two or more `->` or `→` links strung into a pipeline in place of explaining the flow in a sentence; 12 shards.
examples: email memories -> entities -> observations -> open loops
world fact -> condition builder -> CustomerOpsTick -> Charlie customer_ops Tau agent

label: Markdown link to an absolute local path
description: Evidence rendered as `[basename.py](/Users/marcusswift/.../file.py:LINE)` — unclickable for the reader, a citation ritual standing in for quoting the code; all 18 shards.

label: file.ext:LINE citation suffix
description: A line-number anchor appended to a filename as proof-by-pointer, habitual even where the line adds nothing; 9 shards.

label: Bare 'N passed' as the whole proof
description: Test outcomes reduced to a backticked integer with no command output, no failure count, and no statement of what the tests cover; all 18 shards.

label: 'focused' / 'targeted' as pre-emptive cover
description: An adjective attached to the test count that narrows the claim before anyone questions it; 9 shards, and 'focused' alone appears in up to 10 of 50.

label: ruff / py_compile / git diff --check as proof
description: Compilation, lint and whitespace checks reported as if they were evidence of behaviour, including on documentation-only changes; 6 shards.
examples: `ruff check` passed on touched Python files.
`git diff --check` passed for the doc changes.

label: Health-check JSON pasted as deploy proof
description: A raw `{"status":"healthy","version":...}` string dropped in as the last item of the verification block; 4 shards.

label: Backticked commit SHA as identity token
description: Short and full hashes pasted raw in backticks, often without saying what the commit contains; all 18 shards.

label: `command` -> `N passed` pairing
description: The command and its stripped result joined by a bare arrow, in place of showing what ran or what it asserted; 6 shards.

label: Ordinary English words in backticks
description: Status words, counts and plain nouns wrapped in code spans for borrowed authority; backticks are the emphasis device in place of bold, 5-10 spans per message.

label: 'X, not Y' corrective apposition
description: A claim immediately fenced by the rejected alternative; the single most repeated sentence shape in the corpus, present in every shard at 20-46% of messages.
examples: Pricing should come from Stripe, not your DB
a confidence signal, not a sole authorization mechanism
It is execution transport—not project activation and not a second task record.
This is a harness issue, not a meaningful model/compression failure.
The gate—not a component-only test—decides completion.

label: 'rather than' / 'instead of'
description: The same contrast when a bare comma won't fit; Codex prefers 'instead of', and both cluster in the same messages as the comma form; all 18 shards.
examples: To make this operational instead of theoretical
guarded by custom validators rather than a true discriminated component payload model
chooses it, instead of inventing a new provider path

label: Bold used to shout 'not'
description: Bold is reserved almost entirely for the negation rather than for emphasis — in one shard 20 of 74 bold spans are a bare **not**; 9 shards.
examples: we should **not** use your personal GitHub credentials

label: 'So ...' land-the-point restatement
description: A paragraph opening with 'So' that re-says the paragraph above in compressed form, usually as the closer restating the opening verdict; 12 shards.
examples: So the snapshot is coherent and green.
So yes: this materially improves the Playwright suite.
So: **feature, not bug, but we need execution plumbing for the return loop.**
So the short version: the poller found 58 due historical tasks, but none were eligible to run.

label: 'That gives / keeps / lets us ...' value restatement
description: A closing sentence re-asserting the value of what was just described, adding no new information; 6 shards.
examples: That gives us a clean architecture: sandboxing handles environment isolation.
That gives you the final state you want: shared repo, live Hetzner server, customer local clone.
That preserves the human bottleneck for now without making the system guess.

label: "That's the ..." verdict stamp
description: A deictic stamp applied to the sentence just written, converting a statement into a pronouncement; 5 shards.
examples: That's the proof we still need.
That's the cautionary precedent: loading ≠ nudging.

label: 'This proves X; it does not prove Y'
description: A fixed two-clause construction that certifies a result and withdraws half of it in the same sentence; 6 shards.
examples: This proves the schema and deterministic orchestration code; it does not yet prove that the live root model invokes the tool.
This verifies receipt and visibility in Claire—not that Claire has triaged or acted on them yet.
This proves correct routing, not execution of the change-request procedure.
This verifies submission and Sent-folder persistence, not recipient-server delivery or reading.

label: 'does not (yet) prove'
description: The scope-fence verb phrase used to bound every positive claim, whether or not the user asked for the bound; 8 shards.
examples: This does not prove every Charlie capability works.
It does not yet verify Courtney's own self-assignment/account behavior or production.
they do not prove the actual browser route integrates
It does not prove a deployed build or an Alembic upgrade against PostgreSQL.

label: 'remains unverified / remains active' standing debt
description: The standing-qualifier verb attaching an unfinished item to every report; 'remain(s)' appears in 17-29 of 50 in the later shards, often twice in one message.
examples: The verified claim remains limited to the deployed pre-close checkpoint.

label: 'Remaining limitation:' labelled subtraction
description: The last thing the reader sees is a labelled subtraction from the claim just made; 8 shards, and the terminal slot in up to 27 of 50.
regex: (?m)^\s*(?:Remaining limitations?|Remaining proof|Remaining concern|Remaining cleanup|Remaining gap|Remaining meaningful gap|Remaining risk|Residual note|Residual risk|Still unverified|Still unproven|Not yet implemented|Standing limitation|Blocked/unproven|What is not verified enough|What I would not claim yet)\s*:
examples: Remaining limitation: full scheduling still cannot complete because FileMaker contains no `orientation_scheduled` template.
Residual risk: all four deployed staging SHAs differ from local HEAD
Still unverified: whether the current Observation node's emulation produces the same result as a human.

label: 'One caveat:' pre-counted afterthought
description: The real risk demoted to a trailing paragraph announced with a counted noun — always one or two, never three; 9 shards.
examples: One caveat: the script still intentionally bumps to `cpx21` if `INCLUDE_DOCLING=true`
One note: full `npx tsc --noEmit` still fails, but on existing unrelated repo errors.
One important caveat: local files show configured workflows and code owner rules.

label: 'Important distinction:' labelled qualifier
description: A caveat bolted on as a labelled afterthought rather than stated next to the claim it qualifies; 8 shards, with the label rotating through distinction/boundary/nuance/finding.
regex: (?m)^\s*Important(?:\s+(?:distinction|boundary|caveat|note|finding|nuance|precision|pattern|detail|side effect|contract|design rule|billing caveat|process issue|points to settle))?\s*[:.]
examples: Important distinction: these are all session-scoped live tools.
Important boundary: this currently proves the pipeline mechanics, persistence, resumability, deterministic gates, and failure behavior.
Important: I did not mark anything skipped, and I did not greenwash a broken UI into passing.
Important nuance: don't rely on the hourly rollup for the current conversation.

label: 'Note:' / 'Local note:' trailing label
description: The same demotion move under a shorter label, always last, never integrated into the sentence it qualifies; 7 shards.
examples: Note: both repos already have broader unrelated dirty worktree changes.
Local note: there is stashed/uncommitted customer-ops work preserved locally; I did not deploy or discard it.
Quality note: the artifact is now functional and materially useful, but probably still too dense for your “NB only” bar.

label: 'The material blocker is'
description: A named blocker appended as a third coda sentence, using a fixed adjective set that adds weight without adding fact; 4 shards.
regex: \b(?:material blocker|current blocker|remaining blocker|only remaining blocker|The blocker is)\b
examples: The material blocker is that the deployed model currently supports only human `staff` memberships.
Nylas/relay delivery evidence remains the material blocker.
The current blocker is orchestration convergence, not MiniMax capability or Drew's process logic.
The only remaining blocker is that the available browser profile is signed out.

label: 'X, but Y is still not ...' two-clause verdict
description: An assertion immediately halved by a concessive clause, so the win never gets the last word; 7 shards, and the whole message shape in up to 20 of 50.
examples: Erin made material diagnostic progress, but is still ineffective end to end.
The 13 focused tests pass, but they only confirm the reverted baseline—not live effectiveness.
The code is deployed correctly, but the live Kati→Dessi staging workflow is blocked.
The existing admin dashboard tests do pass, but they are insufficient for this requirement.

label: Semicolon welding claim to caveat
description: The claim and its retraction fused into one sentence with a semicolon, avoiding a second sentence and burying the qualifier; 28-31 of 50 in shards 13-18.
examples: Putnam source checkout was unchanged; no push or deployment.
So this was not the test or tool failing; it was the final model call hitting Anthropic rate limit.
The verified claim remains limited to the local three-coder panel; reconciliation and knowledge creation remain unproven.
No further changes were made; the prior claims remain scoped to the observed deployed artifacts.

label: 'Therefore,' pivot to the summarizing claim
description: A connective that introduces a restatement of what the preceding paragraph already established; 5 shards.
examples: Therefore, the precise claim is: each bounded core-system objective set has trustworthy local evidence.
Therefore, deployment is complete; automatic billing for a newly generated model call remains unverified until the later smoke.
Therefore, the manual test-mode release canary is verified.

label: 'X now does Y' present-tense state claim

examples: the fix is not “dumb down the output.”
